Privacy.title: Data and privacy
Privacy.metaDescription: What data Kvaterka.by collects, why, who sees it, and what happens to it.
Privacy.lede: What we collect, why, who sees it, and what happens to it afterward. Written to match how the software actually works, not how pages like this are usually written.

note.p1Rich: Privacy policy in progress. A formal document needs to be drafted by a lawyer practicing in Belarus: it determines the legal basis for processing, the country where data is stored, and retention periods. Until there's an answer, we won't invent retention periods or claim a legal basis.
note.p2: Instead, below is the platform's actual behavior. It's built to hold up under any answer: we collect less than we could.

collect.heading: What's collected
collect.item1: Account: name, email address or phone number, password (stored only as a hash).
collect.item3: Bookings: dates, amounts, check-in and check-out marks.
collect.item6: Identity documents — only if you submit them yourself.

notStored.heading: What we deliberately don't keep
notStored.item1Rich: IP addresses — only as a hash. That's enough to link abuse together, and not enough to reconstruct a history of your movements.
notStored.item2Rich: The session token itself isn't stored. Only its hash sits in the database, so a database leak doesn't hand an attacker your open sessions.
notStored.item3Rich: The action log keeps diffs, not copies. What changed is recorded, not a snapshot of the whole object.
notStored.item4: Guest registration data isn't collected at all.

address.heading: The exact flat address
address.body: Before a booking is confirmed, the map shows only the neighborhood. Publishing the exact address of an empty flat isn't a convenience question — it's a safety question for the host.

id.heading: Identity documents
id.introRich: Their submission is currently switched off and will stay off until a legal decision is made. The system is already built for that switch to be safe:
id.item1: a separate, private storage bucket — the application won't start if it's the same one used for photos;
id.item2Rich: only the reviewer handling the case can read the document — not support, not a moderator, not finance, not even an administrator;
id.item3: every time a document is opened, it's recorded in a log that can't be altered or erased;
id.item4: staff sections only unlock after a second factor, never a password alone.

comms.heading: Who sees the messages
comms.body: The other party — always. Platform staff — only when handling a dispute or complaint. Messages are checked automatically for attempts to move the conversation off the platform, and if part of a message is hidden, the sender is told plainly why.

close.heading: Closing an account
close.p1Rich: The <link>“Account”</link> section lets you close your account. It also lists honestly what happens and what stays — for example, financial records and dispute materials are kept, because erasing them would destroy the other side's evidence.
close.p2: Full data deletion isn't built yet and is waiting on the same legal decision. We won't say “data is deleted” while the bytes are still there.
